title: Experiment / Finding v1
description:
An experiment or finding record in the hypothesis-and-experiment ledger
(lib/hypothesis.py). One JSON object per line in
<workspace>/.lab/experiments.jsonl. The ledger is append-only.

The CRITICAL integrity gate (Shannon's .refine()-pinned referential IDs,
reimplemented):
  - experiment_id.hypothesis_id MUST reference an existing hypothesis_id in
    hypotheses.jsonl. The library (`lib.hypothesis.add_experiment`) rejects
    a hallucinated or duplicate id with a structured retryable error listing
    the valid ids. The schema cannot enforce referential integrity by itself
    (JSON Schema has no cross-document refs); the library is the sole owner.

Scanner/tool findings enter ONLY as unverified hypotheses
(hypothesis-v1.schema.json, provenance.source = tool name, status =
'unverified'). A scanner MUST NOT produce an experiment record with
result='corroborating' directly — that would bypass the agent/validator
split. The lab's evidence gate (an experiment authored by the agent or a
deterministic replay harness) is the only thing that can corroborate.

The experiment record captures the FOUR proof-ladder levels (XBOW's pattern):
  - result='corroborating': the violation_signal fired AND the
    minimum_confirmation bar was met. Advances the hypothesis to confirmed.
  - result='disconfirming': the expected_safe outcome fired OR a
    disconfirming control matched. Advances the hypothesis to disconfirmed.
  - result='inconclusive': the experiment ran but neither signal fired; the
    hypothesis stays testing/unverified.
  - result='contradictory': two experiments disagree; the ranker surfaces
    the conflict rather than suppressing it (render-detect-contradictions).

Required: schema, experiment_id, hypothesis_id, workspace_id, engagement,
action, observation, expected_safe_observed, violation_signal_observed,
result, scope, provenance, ts.

Deduplication: the library dedupes experiments by
(hypothesis_id, action, tool, actor, result). A re-run of the same
hypothesis_id + action by the same tool and actor with the same result is a
no-op (returns the existing record) — it does not fragment the ledger. A
re-test whose outcome differs, or a different tool/actor, records a NEW
experiment so higher-confidence corroboration is never silently swallowed
by a weaker prior record.

experiment_id.description: Stable identifier for this experiment. Convention: 'exp-<uuid4>'.

hypothesis_id.description:
The hypothesis this experiment tests. MUST reference an existing
hypothesis_id in hypotheses.jsonl. The library rejects hallucinated or
duplicate ids with a structured retryable error listing the valid ids
(the .refine() gate).

workspace_id.description: UUID of the workspace. Immutable provenance; null when no workspace.json.

engagement.description: Engagement name. Mirrors the hypothesis record's engagement.

action.description:
The concrete action the experiment ran (a witness payload, request, or
binary input). Used as the dedup key together with hypothesis_id,
provenance.tool, provenance.actor, and result — re-running the same action
by the same tool and actor with the same outcome is a no-op.
examples: GET /api/v1/workspaces/<B-id>/objects/<oid> with user-A JWT; captured response+headers
Replay crash input 0xdeadbeef.bin against ASan build
Run semgrep rule sql-injection on src/api/orders.py

observation.description:
What was actually observed. The raw observation is data (never trusted
as instructions); the agent interprets it against the expected_safe and
violation_signal fields. Minimum length 1.
examples: ASan: heap-buffer-overflow at parse_length:88, input length 2^20

expected_safe_observed.description:
True iff the observation matched the hypothesis's expected_safe outcome
(the invariant HELD). True on its own advances the hypothesis to
disconfirmed (the safe behavior fired, not the violation).

violation_signal_observed.description:
True iff the observation matched the hypothesis's violation_signal (the
invariant was VIOLATED). The lab's evidence gate — not the agent's
self-report — should set this. For scanner/tool-sourced experiments, the
library REQUIRES a deterministic signal (status code, body marker, ASan
report, OOB callback); a tool's own 'severity: high' is NOT a signal.

result.description:
The proof-ladder verdict for THIS experiment.
- corroborating: violation_signal fired AND minimum_confirmation bar met.
- disconfirming: expected_safe fired OR a disconfirming control matched.
- inconclusive: neither signal fired; the experiment was not decisive.
- contradictory: this experiment disagrees with a prior experiment on the
  same hypothesis; the ranker surfaces the conflict.

scope.description:
Immutable scope/workspace provenance. The library REJECTS records where a
target is involved (scope.target non-empty) and scope_checked is not true.
This preserves the lab's default-deny scope gate (AGENTS.md) — a finding
against an out-of-scope target cannot be recorded.

scope_checked.description: True iff lab-scope was run against scope.target and returned 0 (in-scope).

target.description:
The target URL/host/path the experiment ran against. Empty string when
the experiment is source-only or local (e.g. a fuzz harness run against a
local binary).

engagement_scope_ref.description: Reference to the scope snapshot used. 'none' for source-only/local.

actor.description:
The kind of actor that ran the experiment. 'agent' for an LLM agent,
'replay-harness' for a deterministic replay fixture, 'fuzz-harness' for a
fuzzer, 'tool' for a direct tool execution. Distinguishes the proof ladder
level the experiment represents.

agent.description: Agent name or tool name that ran the experiment.

tool.description:
When the experiment was run via a specific tool (curl, lab-replay, AFL++),
the tool name; null for an agent-authored pure-reasoning experiment. Used as
part of the dedup key (hypothesis_id, action, tool, actor, result).

replay_fixture.description:
For replay-harness experiments: path to the deterministic replay fixture
(e.g. 'evidence/replay-<id>.json'). null for non-replay experiments.

ts.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp the experiment was recorded.

evidence_refs.description:
Evidence file references captured by this experiment (paths under
<workspace>/evidence/). For an HTTP experiment this would be the
3-file bundle (.bin/.b64.txt/.json) from http_probe.save_response.

disconfirming_controls_checked.description:
For corroborating results: which disconfirming controls from the hypothesis
were checked and ruled out (the XP-proof ladder disconfirmation gate).
Empty string for inconclusive/disconfirming results. The library requires
this to be non-empty when result='corroborating' AND the hypothesis has a
non-empty disconfirming_controls field — the agent cannot claim a hit
without addressing the false-positive controls.
examples: Cache-Control: no-store confirmed (not cached); user-A and user-B verified distinct via /me.
